```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(SIEVER)
set.seed(1)
# R CMD check rebuilds every vignette under a time limit. The bootstrap in
# this article is run when the vignette is built, so its result is printed
# below, and it is not run again by the check.
during_check <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("_R_CHECK_PACKAGE_NAME_"))
```

## A Measurement Model From R

The interface and public functions use the same analysis services. A script
states the data, item definitions, estimator, and missing-data treatment. It
retains the returned status before interpreting coefficients.

```{r model}
data <- lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939[, paste0("x", 1:9)]
meta <- data.frame(item = names(data), label = names(data),
  construct = rep(c("Visual", "Textual", "Speed"), each = 3L),
  facet = NA_character_, type = "continuous", status = "active",
  reverse = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spec <- sieve_cfa_spec(meta, estimator = "mlr")
result <- sieve_run_model(spec, data)
result$status$code
lavaan::parameterEstimates(result$fit, ci = TRUE)[1:3, c("lhs", "op", "rhs", "est", "ci.lower", "ci.upper")]
```

Factor variances are fixed to one, so all loadings are free. This script
chooses MLR (robust maximum likelihood, for markedly non-normal items), which
uses full information maximum likelihood for missing responses; ML with
FIML and ML on the complete cases are the other continuous choices of the
same `estimator` argument. Under the default `estimator = "auto"`,
continuous items get ML with FIML (DMAR's default: the same estimates as
MLR, with normal-theory standard errors and test statistic), and ordered
items get thresholds and categorical estimation (WLSMV on polychoric
correlations with listwise deletion), so changing an item's type changes
the statistical specification rather than only a display label; a named
estimator such as `"mlr"` treats every item as continuous whatever the
types say.

## Reusing a Fit Through a Session Store

The application estimates the correlated-factors measurement model once
per session: a fit store, `sieve_fit_store()`, keys each fit of that model
by its exact identity
(`sieve_fit_identity()`: the model syntax, the values of the modeled
columns and the respondent rows, the estimator, the missing data
treatment, the identification, the sampling design and the engine
versions), and the CFA, Items and Validity pages, the measurement model
behind the Reliability page's factor scores, and the assistant reuse an
identical fit instead of fitting it again. The store holds those fits
alone: the exploratory, item response, structural, bifactor, invariance
and Optimizer models are fit where they are requested, and the methods
draft fits its own CFA. In a script, `sieve_fit_cfa()` given a store keys
its fits the same way. Two fits are never equated by
approximation; another estimator, another row set or a changed value of a
modeled column is another identity.

```{r fit-store}
store <- sieve_fit_store()
first <- sieve_fit_cfa(data, meta, store = store)
again <- sieve_fit_cfa(data, meta, store = store)
identical(first, again)
length(store$entries)
other <- sieve_fit_cfa(data, meta, store = store, estimator = "ml")
length(store$entries)

id <- sieve_fit_identity(sieve_cfa_spec(meta, reserved = names(data)), data)
changed <- data
changed$x1[1] <- changed$x1[1] + 1
identical(id, sieve_fit_identity(sieve_cfa_spec(meta, reserved = names(data)), changed))
```

In the application the store is emptied whenever data are loaded and is
never written into a project; a reused fit enters no measured rate and the
session script records which page fit it and when.

## Reliability and Uncertainty

The Reliability tab's default is Robust omega (observed denominator): the
squared sum of the one-factor loadings over the variance of the
unit-weighted composite, estimated from the unrestricted covariance matrix
(Kelley & Pornprasertmanit, 2016, where it is introduced as hierarchical
omega). Its interval is a percentile bootstrap for continuous items and a
BCa bootstrap for ordered or binary items, 10000 replications by default,
run on request. `sieve_reliability_spec()` resolves the request; with
`run_bootstrap = FALSE` the point estimate is computed and the resampling
is left pending, which is what the tab shows before Run the bootstrap is
pressed. Omega (model-implied denominator) with DMAR's default interval
(the MLR (sandwich) standard error, its limits formed on the logit scale) is returned beside it
(the `model_` columns). The request's defaults are DMAR's: `missing =
"fiml"` and, through `ci_method = "recommended"`, DMAR's default interval
for each coefficient.

```{r reliability}
items <- paste0("x", 1:3)
types <- stats::setNames(rep("continuous", 3L), items)
reliability_spec <- sieve_reliability_spec(items, types = types, construct = "Visual",
  missing = "fiml", run_bootstrap = FALSE)
reliability_spec$coefficient
reliability_spec$uncertainty$status
reliability <- sieve_reliability_construct(data, reliability_spec, alpha = FALSE)
shown <- c("construct", "coefficient", "omega", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "interval",
  "model_omega", "model_lower", "model_upper", "model_interval")
sieve_reliability_table(list(Visual = reliability))[, shown]
```

The bootstrap itself, DMAR's counted bootstrap, with a seed and a small
`B` so that this vignette builds in seconds (the application
never lowers `B` to shorten a wait, Hesterberg, 2015); the table reports
the replications attempted and used. The recorded call is the DMAR call,
with its seed, `B`, interval method, level, missing data treatment and
`ncpus`.

```{r reliability-bootstrap, eval = !during_check}
boot_spec <- sieve_reliability_spec(items, types = types, construct = "Visual",
  missing = "fiml", B = 400L, seed = 1)
boot <- sieve_reliability_construct(data, boot_spec, alpha = FALSE)
sieve_reliability_table(list(Visual = boot))[, c("construct", "omega", "ci_lower",
  "ci_upper", "interval", "boot_attempted", "boot_used")]
```

Omega describes the defined composite under its measurement model, and
what is robust is the denominator only, against misspecification of the
total variance; the numerator comes from the one-factor model under either
denominator. The interval does not certify the construct's meaning or
justify substituting a different set of answered items for each respondent.

## Scoring a Construct

The operational score of a construct, as the Reliability tab's Operational
Score Specification keeps it, is either a composite computed by
`sieve_composite_score()` (the mean of the answered items, or that mean
prorated to the sum, under a minimum answered count or proportion, with
each respondent's eligibility and answered count) or a Bartlett or
regression factor score read from the fitted measurement model. Nothing is
imputed across respondents, and the returned policy states the rule in a
sentence.

```{r composite}
scored <- data
scored$x2[1:5] <- NA
visual <- sieve_composite_score(scored, items, min_count = 2L)
table(answered = visual$answered, scored = visual$eligible)
visual$policy$missing
head(visual$scores)
```

An available-response composite is an operational score: a respondent who
answered two items is scored on different content from one who answered
three, and a reliability coefficient estimated for the complete composite
does not describe that procedure. The model-based alternative, a factor
score estimated under full information maximum likelihood without
proration, is the next section.

## Scores With Their Respondents

`sieve_factor_score_record()` returns Bartlett or regression scores with a
person-level interval for every input row, conditioning on the fitted
parameters as known.

```{r scores}
scores <- sieve_factor_score_record(result$fit, method = "Bartlett", data = data,
  original_rows = seq_len(nrow(data)), conf_level = .95)
head(scores$uncertainty)
```

Score rows retain the corresponding data-row and original-row references.
An observation omitted by the estimator has no invented score. For categorical
ML scores, an extreme response pattern can have no finite ML estimate;
empirical Bayes modal scoring answers a different, explicitly labeled question.

## Calibration and Validation

The public split service and the CV and Invariance tab use the same engine.
It samples only rows complete on every included item, even when the selected
continuous-item estimator otherwise supports full information maximum
likelihood. The two subsets are disjoint; they still belong to the same
study, and prior exposure to the validation observations is not erased.

```{r cross-validation}
split <- sieve_cross_validate(data, meta, holdout = .4, seed = 113,
  estimator = "mlr")
split$table
split$xval
split$rel
stopifnot(length(intersect(split$calibration_rows, split$validation_rows)) == 0L)
split$rng
```

`eligible_rows`, `calibration_rows`, and `validation_rows` refer to positions
in the input data before complete-case removal. Keep these references when
linking a split to respondent records. The discrepancy compares the
calibration model's covariance with the validation covariance, followed by
the validation model's own minimized discrepancy; their difference is
reported as shrinkage. This covariance comparison is unavailable for ordered
items. Reliability follows the Reliability tab's targets: Robust omega
(observed denominator) as point estimates for the two halves, since its
interval is a bootstrap that is not run for the split, and Omega
(model-implied denominator) with its MLR (sandwich) SE interval in each half and
for the difference. The service refuses clustered or repeated sampling
designs because it does not implement design-aware splitting or
uncertainty for those designs.

The returned RNG record stores the seed actually used and all three
`RNGkind()` settings. A supplied seed preserves the caller's random number
stream. With `seed = NULL`, the caller's stream advances by one draw to choose
the recorded seed. Restore the recorded settings and supply that seed to
repeat the split in another session. `sieve_analyze("cross_validation", ...)`
also exposes this service and returns the result as a `siever_analysis`
object that keeps the request hash and the engine versions with it.

### A Reservation Drawn Before Development

A split drawn after the full data were examined is internal assessment.
The evaluation can be more than that when the validation rows were
reserved before the structure and the items were examined and the model
evaluated on them was frozen before the evaluation (Browne, 2000). In the
application the reservation is made on the Screening page's Observations
panel and evaluated once on the CV and Invariance page; from a script,
`sieve_holdout_sizes()` states what a proportion would reserve,
`sieve_holdout_draw()` draws the rows by a seed (optionally within the
strata of a grouping variable), and `sieve_cross_validate()` takes them as
`validation_rows`, given rather than drawn, so `holdout` and `seed` are
unused and `rng` is `NULL`.

```{r reservation}
sieve_holdout_sizes(nrow(data), proportion = .3)
reserved <- sieve_holdout_draw(seq_len(nrow(data)), proportion = .3, seed = 1)
given <- sieve_cross_validate(data, meta, validation_rows = reserved$rows,
  estimator = "mlr")
c(n_cal = given$n_cal, n_val = given$n_val)
is.null(given$rng)
given$rel[, c("Construct", "Coefficient", "Calibration", "Validation", "Difference")]
```

## The Session Download

The Reproducible Code page leads with Report saved analyses, a report
from the analyses recorded in the session that runs nothing, and offers
Run a new analysis and draft, which refits and says so. Its
Download script and inputs (.tar.gz) archive contains `siever_session.R`,
the companion input file `siever_inputs.rds` (read back by
`sieve_replay_read()` against its recorded hash), and a `README.txt`.
Unpack the archive into one private directory, set the working directory
there, and run `source("siever_session.R")`. Data are stored once by
content hash. State-changing expressions run
in order, with their resulting item definitions, responses, and respondent
rows checked against the recorded revision. The script calls exported
SIEVER functions and names its package requirement.

A project file is the private restorable study. A study bundle is a separate
sharing product: its fresh sharing project keeps the item columns with the
current item assignments, reversals, scoring policies and sampling
declaration, without removed respondents, identifier and auxiliary columns,
private wording and narratives, analyses, project history, or
external-review records. Read the bundle's `README.txt` and `manifest.R`,
which state what it includes and excludes, before sharing it.

## Citing What Was Run

Every report and draft the application writes ends with a bibliography of
the methods actually used, from a verified registry.
`sieve_method_references()` lists every citation SIEVER can make with the
claim it supports and where it applies; each analysis record carries the
keys of the methods its specification used, and
`sieve_method_bibliography()` formats the deduplicated entries of those
keys and of the software they ran in, with the versions in use. A method
is never cited because it exists in the registry, only because an analysis
used it, and an entry whose record could not be verified is left out of
every export and named in the `omitted` attribute.

```{r references}
refs <- sieve_method_references()
table(refs$kind)
cat(strwrap(refs$claim[refs$key == "omega_robust"], width = 76), sep = "\n")
sieve_method_bibliography(c("cfa", "mlr", "fiml", "omega_robust"), software = FALSE)
```

## Reading an Analysis Result

`sieve_analyze()` offers named headless services for the major analyses and
returns a `siever_analysis` object. `summary()`, `as.data.frame()`, and `confint()`
inspect the stored result. The object carries `schema_version`, the version of
its fields (1), and `intervals`, one table of every confidence interval the
result holds, filled when the analysis runs: the table and row, the estimate
and its standard error, the limits, the level, the side (two-sided, or the
upper bound of HTMT), the method, the number of cases used, and, for a row
without limits, the reason. A DMAR refusal (from `irt`, `htmt`, `ave`, or
`content`) is returned as a failed analysis with DMAR's reason rather than
stopping the script. `print()` lists the interval tables and `confint()` reads
its limits from `intervals`, following one rule by interval type. With `level = NULL`, the default, it
returns the stored limits at the level each was stored at. Another level is
computed only for a Wald interval (lavaan parameters with standard or robust
standard errors, the Wald intervals of omega, H, and alpha, and factor score
intervals), from the stored estimate and standard error on the scale the
interval was formed on, after the stored limits are reproduced at their own
level; the returned matrix records `conf_level`, `interval_method`, and
`source`, which is `"stored"` or
`"computed from the stored estimate and standard error"`. Bootstrap,
profile likelihood, order-statistic, exact binomial, and noncentral
chi-square (RMSEA, ECVI) limits are refused at another level, with the call
that reruns the analysis at that level; for RMSEA that is
`options(sieve.rmsea_conf_level = )`. One-sided bounds, such as HTMT's, are
refused at every level, naming the column that holds them. For a dependent
design, use a supported resolved model specification; the convenience
dispatcher refuses to pretend that dependent rows are independent
observations.

## Finding the Analysis Service

The functions below provide the numerical services behind the corresponding
panels; with `run_app()` and the functions `?SIEVER` names, they are every
function SIEVER exports, and `help(package = "SIEVER")` lists them with their
help pages. Calls to DMAR, lavaan, and psych use those packages' documented public
interfaces. SIEVER's display rounding is separate from returned estimates.
Read a service's input, missing-response, model, and sampling assumptions
before interpreting its result; a direct engine call uses that engine's
assumptions. A row bootstrap does not account for clustered observations.

| Workflow | Public service |
|---|---|
| Prepare data and item definitions | `sieve_specification_template()`, `sieve_prepare_study()` |
| Descriptive summaries | `base::mean()`, `stats::sd()`, `stats::median()`, `DMAR::skewness()`, `DMAR::kurtosis()`; floor/ceiling percentages use the observed minimum/maximum among nonmissing responses, and missingness uses all input rows |
| Response-pattern screening | `sieve_response_screens()` |
| Validation reservation | `sieve_holdout_sizes()`, `sieve_holdout_draw()` |
| Correlation basis and dimensionality | `sieve_retention_cor()`, `sieve_retention_evidence()`, `sieve_correlation_heatmap()` |
| EFA pattern, simple structure, number of factors, and model fit | `DMAR::fa_exploratory()`, `DMAR::factor_count()`, `DMAR::simple_structure()`, `sieve_efa_factor_plot()`, `sieve_efa_fit_by_k()` |
| Item and nested-facet review | `sieve_item_diagnostics()`, `sieve_item_rest()`, `sieve_facet_item_rest()` |
| Content coverage of the included items | `sieve_item_coverage()`, `sieve_coverage_change()` |
| Constrained item-set search and ordering | `sieve_optimize_items()`, `sieve_order_candidates()` |
| CFA and structural alternatives | `sieve_cfa_spec()`, `sieve_run_model()`, `sieve_fit_cfa()`, `sieve_compare_structures()`, `sieve_structures_table()` |
| Fit index changes along a sequence of nested models | `sieve_fit_compare()` |
| Reuse of an identical fit | `sieve_fit_store()`, `sieve_fit_identity()` |
| Modification indices and residuals | `sieve_modification_indices()`, `sieve_residual_pairs()` |
| Model-based bootstrap and latent-correlation boundaries | `sieve_bollen_stine()`, `sieve_latent_bound()` |
| Reliability, intervals, and operational scores | `sieve_reliability_spec()`, `sieve_reliability_construct()`, `sieve_reliability_table()`, `sieve_composite_score()`, `sieve_score_policy()`, `sieve_score_policy_sensitivity()` |
| Reliability precision planning | `sieve_plan_congeneric()`, `DMAR::ss_aipe_reliability()` |
| Model-derived total or weighted composites | `sieve_model_composite()` |
| Bifactor indices and counted intervals | `sieve_fit_bifactor()`, `sieve_bifactor_bootstrap()` |
| Expert ratings: I-CVI, modified kappa, CVR, S-CVI | `DMAR::content_validity_index()`; scale summaries are attributes `s_cvi_ave` and `s_cvi_ua` |
| AVE, HTMT, and method-factor sensitivity | `DMAR::average_variance_extracted()`, `DMAR::htmt()`, `sieve_run_method_factor()` |
| Single-factor screen and marker adjustment | `DMAR::common_method_single_factor()`, `DMAR::common_method_marker()`, `sieve_marker_sensitivity()` |
| Stated criterion predictions | `sieve_validity_estimate()`, `sieve_validity_evidence()` |
| IRT parameters and information | `DMAR::irt_grm()`, `DMAR::irt_information()`, and the evidence functions `sieve_irt_parameter_evidence()`, `sieve_irt_category_probabilities()`, `sieve_irt_information_bands()`, `sieve_irt_empirical_traces()`, `sieve_irt_residual_pairs()`, `sieve_irt_bivariate_table()` |
| Structural paths, indirect effects, and R-squared | `sieve_run_structural()`, `sieve_indirect_mc()`, `sieve_R2_intervals()`, `sieve_outcome_scale()` |
| Multiple imputation sensitivity for ordered items | `sieve_mi_plan()`, `sieve_mi_model()` |
| Internal calibration and validation, and evaluation on reserved rows | `sieve_cross_validate()` |
| Invariance, partial constraints, and interpretation | `sieve_fit_invariance()`, `sieve_invariance_interpret()`, `sieve_anchor_sensitivity()`, `sieve_ordinal_fit_impact()`, `lavaan::lavTestScore()` |
| Noninvariance impact and alignment | `DMAR::dmacs()`, `DMAR::measurement_alignment()` |
| Longitudinal models and contrasts | `sieve_longitudinal_spec()`, `sieve_run_longitudinal()`, `sieve_longitudinal_compare()`, `sieve_longitudinal_contrasts()` |
| Scores, scoring syntax, and fixed references | `sieve_factor_score_record()`, `sieve_scoring_code()`, `sieve_construct_norms()`, `sieve_norm_freeze()`, `sieve_norm_read()`, `sieve_norm_apply()`, `sieve_norm_transform_limits()` |
| Local wording and keying review | `sieve_wording_checks()`, `sieve_reverse_balance()` |
| The levels of the intervals | `sieve_default_conf_level()`, `sieve_default_rmsea_conf_level()` |
| The methods registry, bibliography, and methods draft | `sieve_method_references()`, `sieve_method_bibliography()`, `sieve_methods_draft()` |
| Model diagrams | `sieve_diagram_spec()`, `sieve_draw_diagram()`, `sieve_export_diagram()` |
| Projects and what they hold | `sieve_project_write()`, `sieve_project_read()`, `sieve_project_analyses()`, `sieve_project_report()`, `sieve_project_decisions()` |
| The session script and its replay | `sieve_session_write()`, `sieve_replay()`, `sieve_replay_read()`, `sieve_replay_bind()`, `sieve_replay_verify()`, `sieve_replay_engine_check()` |

For example, the corrected item-rest calculation keeps its pair count and
reason when an estimate is undefined. A criterion prediction reads an
existing interval against a stated expectation and does not turn agreement
into a validity verdict. The marker-variable adjustment of Lindell and
Whitney (2001) is read over several values of the marker correlation, with
its constant method effect assumption stated.

```{r item-and-criterion-services}
sieve_item_rest(data, paste0("x", 1:3))
criterion <- sieve_validity_estimate(data$x1, data$x2, conf_level = .90)
estimates <- data.frame(construct = "Visual item", criterion = "Second item",
  r = criterion$r, lower = criterion$lower, upper = criterion$upper,
  n = criterion$n, p = criterion$p, reason = criterion$reason)
expectations <- data.frame(construct = "Visual item", criterion = "Second item",
  kind = "directional", sign = 1, min_abs = NA_real_, bound = NA_real_)
sieve_validity_evidence(estimates, expectations)
scoring <- sieve_scoring_code(meta, values = "processed")
scoring$name_map

construct_scores <- data.frame(
  Visual  = sieve_composite_score(data, paste0("x", 1:3))$scores,
  Textual = sieve_composite_score(data, paste0("x", 4:6))$scores,
  Speed   = sieve_composite_score(data, paste0("x", 7:9))$scores
)
sieve_marker_sensitivity(cor(construct_scores), marker_r = c(.05, .10), n = nrow(data))
```

In a standalone ledger, `meta$status[meta$item == "x1"] <- "parked"` excludes
that item from later calls while retaining its response column (the
specification file and the interface say included and excluded; the ledger
stores `"active"` and `"parked"`). Set the status to `"active"` to include it
again. The application's item and respondent action histories are preserved
through its project and session workflows; changing a separate data frame
does not create those records.

## References

Browne, M. W. (2000). Cross-validation methods. *Journal of Mathematical
Psychology, 44*, 108--132.

Hesterberg, T. C. (2015). What teachers should know about the bootstrap:
Resampling in the undergraduate statistics curriculum. *The American
Statistician, 69*, 371--386.

Kelley, K., & Pornprasertmanit, S. (2016). Confidence intervals for
population reliability coefficients: Evaluation of methods,
recommendations, and software for composite measures. *Psychological
Methods, 21*, 69--92.

Lindell, M. K., & Whitney, D. J. (2001). Accounting for common method
variance in cross-sectional research designs. *Journal of Applied
Psychology, 86*, 114--121.
